name: Disk Hoard · Talos
purpose: Absorbed by Talos's Hoard. Compatibility identity only; no standalone server. Measures what fills the user's disks, knows which folders are regenerable junk (caches, node_modules, build output, temp files) and can clean them: to the Recycle Bin, permanently with explicit confirmation, or through a reviewable PowerShell script. It also splits a folder into ZIPs that each stay under a size limit (upload sites with a per-file cap), cutting a file bigger than the limit into raw .zip.001 volumes.
notes: Absorbed by Talos's Hoard: https://github.com/Luissalet/TalosHoard. Launch the merged app explicitly; this identity preserves existing family calls and data. Standard library only: any Python 3.9+ runs both the app and the MCP bridge, so Faustus's own interpreter is enough. The bridge starts the app itself when it is not running. The UI opens with a token in the URL; the bridge reads the same token from data/mcp-token. Deleting through the assistant goes to the Recycle Bin unless it says mode='permanent' with confirm=true, and drive roots, the user profile, Windows and anything the catalog marks 'do not touch' are always refused. Zip splitting (disk_zip_plan, disk_zip_split, disk_zip_status, disk_zip_cancel) never changes the source folder unless too_large='move' is used with confirm=true; it refuses to write into drive roots, Windows, Program Files or the profile root, never writes inside the source folder, and leaves no half-written part when cancelled. Ollama backups (disk_ollama_backups is read only; disk_ollama_free defaults to dry_run and needs confirm=true) only ever frees items the detector verified as safe, refuses while Ollama has models loaded or a pull/run is active, removes migration backups with 'ollama rm' and logs every action to data/ollama-free-audit.jsonl.
